title: 9. Powers and Functions of Chief Minister

blocks.content: The Chief Minister is the real executive authority (de facto executive) of the state, while the Governor is the nominal executive authority (de jure executive).

rows: Appointed by the President of India
Appointed by the Governor (Leader of majority party)
Acts on the advice of the Council of Ministers
Heads, guides, directs, and controls the Council of Ministers

items: Distinguish Article 164 (Appointment of CM and Ministers) from Article 167 (Duties of CM to furnish administrative information to the Governor).
Remember that the CM serves as the Vice-Chairman of the concerned Zonal Council by rotation for a term of one year at a time.
The Governor can dismiss a state minister only on the specific advice of the Chief Minister, not independently.

blocks.title: Key Takeaways
items: The Chief Minister is the real executive authority (de facto executive) at the state level, while the Governor is the nominal executive (de jure executive).
Under Article 164, the Chief Minister is appointed by the Governor, and other ministers are appointed by the Governor on the advice of the Chief Minister.
Article 167 defines the duties of the Chief Minister as a communicator between the Council of Ministers and the Governor.
The Chief Minister advises the Governor on the appointment of key state officials such as the Advocate General, Chairman/Members of SPSC, and State Election Commissioner.
The Chief Minister acts as the Chairman of the State Planning Board and represents the state in the Governing Council of NITI Aayog and the Inter-State Council.
